seoTitle: Reactivate a Suspended User in Google Workspace
metaDescription: Restore access for a suspended Google Workspace user through the Admin Console, whether the suspension was for inactivity, policy, or payment issues.
intro: A suspended Google Workspace account locks a user out of Gmail, Drive, Meet, Calendar, and every other tool tied to their login, whether the cause was inactivity, a policy violation, or a billing problem. Only a domain admin can lift that suspension, and the fix itself takes under a minute once you know where the Status column lives in the Users list. This guide walks through the Admin Console path from sign-in to a restored, active account, aimed at admins and IT teams managing business email under a custom domain.

steps.heading: Sign in with an administrator account
steps.body: Go to admin.google.com and sign in. Google shows an explicit reminder here that you need an administrator account for a managed service like Google Workspace or Cloud Identity — a regular user login won't get you past this screen, and if your organization has multiple admin identities, the account chooser lists each one so you can pick the right domain before continuing.

image.caption: The Google sign-in screen for admin.google.com, with a reminder that an administrator account is required and a list of available accounts to choose from.

steps.heading: Land on the Admin Console home screen
steps.body: After signing in you're dropped on the Admin Console home page, with a "Manage Workspace" section showing Users and Billing summary cards and a full navigation sidebar on the left covering Directory, Devices, Apps, Security, Data, and Reporting. This is the control center for the whole domain, but for reactivating one user you only need a single item from that sidebar.

steps.heading: Open Directory, then Users
steps.body: In the left sidebar, expand Directory to reveal Users, Groups, Target audiences, Organisational units, and related settings. Click Users — this is where every account on your domain lives, active and suspended alike, and it's the same screen you'd use to add, remove, or bulk-update accounts.

image.caption: The Admin Console sidebar with Directory expanded, showing the path to Home, Dashboard, Directory, Devices, and Apps.

steps.heading: Find the suspended user in the list
steps.body: The Users page shows every account with columns for Name, Email, Status, Last sign-in, and Email usage. A suspended account's Status column reads something like "Suspended by admin" with a timestamp, standing out clearly next to accounts marked Active. Searching the box above the table by name or domain keyword narrows a long directory down fast if you're managing more than a handful of users.

image.caption: The Users list with one account showing "Suspended by admin" in the Status column, next to two other accounts marked Active.

steps.heading: Open the account and unsuspend it
steps.body: Click the suspended user's name to open their account page, which shows the same suspended status along with details on when it happened. Look for the "Restore user" or "Unsuspend" action — on most Admin Console layouts it sits near the top of the account page or under a more-options menu — and confirm. The Status column updates back to Active as soon as the change saves.

steps.heading: Confirm access is restored
steps.body: Have the user try signing back into Gmail or another Workspace app, or check their Last sign-in timestamp update in the Users list yourself. Unsuspending restores access to their existing Gmail, Drive, Meet, and Calendar data rather than recreating the account, so nothing they had before the suspension should be missing — assuming it wasn't separately deleted, which is a different action from suspension.

steps.heading: Know why accounts get suspended, to avoid a repeat
steps.body: The three usual triggers are prolonged inactivity, a policy violation flagged by Google or an admin, and an unresolved billing issue on the Workspace subscription. If billing was the cause, check that the payment method on file is current before you unsuspend, since a subscription still in arrears can suspend the account right back. For inactivity-triggered suspensions, a quick reminder to sign in periodically is usually enough to prevent a repeat.

faq.question: Why was a Google Workspace user account suspended?
faq.answer: Common reasons include prolonged inactivity, a policy violation, or unresolved payment issues on the Workspace subscription — the account's Status column in the Users list usually indicates which.

faq.question: Who can reactivate a suspended Workspace user?
faq.answer: Reactivation is done by a domain admin through the Google Admin Console's Directory > Users page, not by the individual user themselves.

faq.question: Will reactivating the account restore all their data?
faq.answer: Unsuspending restores access to the account's existing Gmail, Drive, Meet, and Calendar data, assuming the data wasn't separately deleted — suspension and deletion are different admin actions.

faq.question: How do I avoid future suspensions on Workspace accounts?
faq.answer: Keep the subscription's payment method current, encourage regular sign-ins to avoid inactivity flags, and review policy violation notices promptly rather than letting them lapse into a suspension.

faq.question: Does a suspended account lose its custom domain email?
faq.answer: No — the email address tied to the custom domain stays associated with the account. Access is simply blocked in the Status column until an admin unsuspends it.
